summary: Acceptance time: the submissions-JSON acceptanceDateTime (suffix Z) is the Eastern wall time shifted by the ET->UTC offset twice (+8 h EDT, +10 h EST)
decision: Acceptance time: the submissions-JSON acceptanceDateTime (suffix Z) is the Eastern wall time shifted by the ET->UTC offset twice (+8 h EDT, +10 h EST). Two UTC->ET conversions reproduce the SGML ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME to the second (verified 2026-10-23 on 2002, 2004, 2012, 2016, 2020, 2023 and 2026 filings). The SGML header is used whenever a download carries it (every 8-K full submission); JSON times are quality A only while the header checks agree (mismatch <= 1%), else quality C. Pre-2002 filings carry midnight placeholders -> quality B, assumed 17:30 ET. Unit test against a recorded header fixture.
why: SPEC.md asks to verify timezone semantics on a sample.

decision: Common cohort = events eligible for every compared rung: price features present, accounting available (any point-in-time XBRL fact or SUE), text sections present (and embeddings for L5/L7). decision: Decision rule: heads train with class-balanced weights; their probabilities are prior-corrected to true frequencies, temperature-calibrated on an inner training slice, and the cost-balanced decision argmax p / prior (Laplace-smoothed; a class absent from training is never predicted) is applied once.

decision: Early stopping, calibration and clip bounds use an inner, time-ordered slice of the training fold; hyperparameters are selected on walk-forward validation blocks.

summary: Release-EPS parser fixes from real releases: values are read after the label cell (keeps "(0.15)" negatives), a lone "Diluted" label line is joined with the numeric line below it (Apple 2020-21 layout), block elements in
decision: Release-EPS parser fixes from real releases: values are read after the label cell (keeps "(0.15)" negatives), a lone "Diluted" label line is joined with the numeric line below it (Apple 2020-21 layout), block elements inside table cells stay inline, a sentence reporting "$2.71 GAAP and $2.27 non-GAAP" yields the GAAP value, and 52/53-week fiscal years ending in the first week of a month map to the previous month. Live smoke: 25 releases, 23 parsed, 21 exact XBRL matches (the 2 sign errors were fixed after that run).

summary: Correction to D-003
decision: Correction to D-003. At pilot scale (8,789 header comparisons) the submissions-JSON acceptance time follows two conventions: ~70% double-shifted, ~30% true UTC (differences of exactly -4 h / -5 h), mixed within filing agents, hours, forms and years. The SGML header is now read for every filing (8-Ks: full submission; 10-K/10-Q: first 20 KB of the full submission, cached under a separate key). JSON-only times fall to quality C via the existing verification gate (mismatch 30% > 1%).
why: Measured on the pilot; the 2002-2026 spot sample in D-003 happened to contain only double-shifted filings.

summary: Release-EPS parser, second round from 2,086 pilot comparisons with XBRL (65% match before): a "(" marks a negative even when ")" is in the next cell; share-count rows are skipped; rows under annual / outlook / guidance h
decision: Release-EPS parser, second round from 2,086 pilot comparisons with XBRL (65% match before): a "(" marks a negative even when ")" is in the next cell; share-count rows are skipped; rows under annual / outlook / guidance headings and full-year prose are skipped unless the context names the quarter; "continuing operations" EPS is kept for QA but is not usable for SUE (XBRL EarningsPerShareDiluted is total EPS); table candidates are scored (income-statement heading +2, quarter context +1) instead of taking the first match; guidance ranges, discontinued-operations rows and "impact of an item" sentences are skipped. Pilot (40 firms, 2012-2026): match with the first-reported XBRL value 65% -> 77% overall, 78.5% at usable confidence (1,929 releases); remaining gaps include XBRL restatements and unit errors.

summary: Tuning screen for full: Optuna trials score the 3 most recent walk-forward folds with a time-stratified subsample of at most 30,000 training rows per fold (a budget-driven deviation from SPEC.md v5 §9.4, which does not p
decision: Tuning screen for full: Optuna trials score the 3 most recent walk-forward folds with a time-stratified subsample of at most 30,000 training rows per fold (a budget-driven deviation from SPEC.md v5 §9.4, which does not prescribe a screen; v5 is the single source of truth, so the earlier v3 wording is not a justification); every reported default and tuned result is then refit on all training rows of every fold. Pilot keeps the unscreened search.
why: Pilot S11 took 19.5 min for 10k events / 2 folds; a linear projection put full S11 at ~10-15 h.

summary: Adversarial validation is reported twice: with all features and with firm-level features only (market-wide mkt_* and calendar fields removed)
decision: Adversarial validation is reported twice: with all features and with firm-level features only (market-wide mkt_* and calendar fields removed). Date-level features fingerprint each date, so the all-feature AUC is trivially ~1.0 (pilot: 1.0); the firm-level AUC is the interpretable covariate-shift diagnostic.

summary: Adversarial validation also records the five features that separate train from validation (gain share), and the report reads a high AUC as covariate shift, not leakage
decision: Adversarial validation also records the five features that separate train from validation (gain share), and the report reads a high AUC as covariate shift, not leakage. Pilot: the firm-level AUC stays ~1.0. In the L6 matrix the drivers are TF-IDF SVD components (filing vocabulary drifts over time; tokens are letters-only, so year numbers are not features); on the structured features alone the drivers are level fundamentals (log assets, log revenue, beta, ROA) that trend within each of the 40 firms (AUC 0.999). Both are point-in-time information, not leakage (the leakage audit and its four planted leaks pass).

summary: Early-era real-data run (2000-2004; AAPL, XOM, AXP, IBM, PFE, INTC; 361 filings, 317 events) found two defects that the pilot (2012+) and fixtures could not
decision: Early-era real-data run (2000-2004; AAPL, XOM, AXP, IBM, PFE, INTC; 361 filings, 317 events) found two defects that the pilot (2012+) and fixtures could not. (1) For AXP, IBM and PFE every 10-K's MD&A is by reference to Exhibit 13, and the EX-13 finder knew only "Management's Discussion and Analysis of ..." (annual reports use "FINANCIAL REVIEW", "Management Discussion"); 18 of 36 early 10-Ks had ~250 characters of MD&A. EX-13 now also accepts those line-anchored titles (EX-13 only, so main-document parsing is unchanged); after the fix 36 of 36 have 20k-190k characters. The same gap affected 18 of 668 pilot 10-Ks (2.7%); those 6 firms were re-parsed. (2) Fiscal Q4 releases quote full-year EPS and the parser can pick it (AXP $5.42, XOM $3.23 as "quarter"). New point-in-time check flag_suspect_annual: a Q4 value above 2x the firm's largest earlier quarterly EPS (>= 2 earlier values) becomes suspect_annual (QA only, never a SUE input). On the pilot it withholds 45 of 2,045 releases (35 disagreed with XBRL, 10 agreed: conservative) and raises the XBRL match rate from 78.5% to 79.8%. Residual: it needs two earlier quarters, so a firm's first releases are not covered (XOM 2003 here).
why: Hard rule 12 (verify before use); audit finding H3.

summary: Early-era data limits, expected and handled per spec rather than defects: filings before ~2003 have no SGML acceptance time in a usable form (quality B date-only or C), so 2000-2002 events are largely B/C (T_info exclude
decision: Early-era data limits, expected and handled per spec rather than defects: filings before ~2003 have no SGML acceptance time in a usable form (quality B date-only or C), so 2000-2002 events are largely B/C (T_info excludes C); SUE is unavailable before about 2004-05 (release-EPS history of 8 quarters needs several years of parsed releases and XBRL only starts in 2009); legacy 8-K item codes map with no OTHER_OR_UNMAPPED. The common cohort is therefore mostly 2009+ (D-020); the 2000-2008 events enter only the maximum-available cohort.

summary: Reproducibility: all 26 ChronoBERT vintages are pinned to Hub commit SHAs and S14 refuses an unpinned revision; requirements.lock records the tested versions; the notebook installs exact pins for the add-on libraries (co
decision: Reproducibility: all 26 ChronoBERT vintages are pinned to Hub commit SHAs and S14 refuses an unpinned revision; requirements.lock records the tested versions; the notebook installs exact pins for the add-on libraries (core runtime libraries are never reinstalled) and falls back package by package with a printed warning. Tests assert every model has a 40-hex revision and that the notebook pins equal the lock file.

summary: sec.s05_max_wall_hours (notebook default 8, config default 0 = unlimited): S05 stops cleanly after that many hours with StageIncomplete (recorded as "incomplete", not "failed"); running the same cell again skips finished
decision: sec.s05_max_wall_hours (notebook default 8, config default 0 = unlimited): S05 stops cleanly after that many hours with StageIncomplete (recorded as "incomplete", not "failed"); running the same cell again skips finished firms. Colab sessions can disconnect during the ~9 h download; every finished firm is already on Drive, so nothing is lost either way. The key is outside the S05 stage hash.

summary: Owner decision (2026-10-23): keep 500 firms and analyse the index buckets
decision: Owner decision (2026-10-23): keep 500 firms and analyse the index buckets. The universe stays HF 10-K corpus ∩ our OHLCV, S&P 500 members first (about 353 eligible over 2000-2026), then a seeded, sector-stratified fill of non-members (about 147). Every firm carries sp_bucket = SP500 (ever a member in the study window per the pinned fja05680 list) or NonSP500 (not found in that list: the list is incomplete in early years, so this is not "verified never a member"); point-in-time membership on the decision date is reported alongside and is never a feature. Results are reported for SP500, NonSP500 and Combined: bucket composition; the combined models' walk-forward, development-holdout and locked-test scores per bucket; bucket-only models (same rung, head, tuned parameters and folds) against the pooled model on identical rows (paired month-block bootstrap); Track A CARs and CAR paths; SUE drift (own FDR family drift_sp_bucket; Track A buckets in track_a_car_sp_bucket, so the pre-registered families are unchanged); the backtest with the same frozen model and thresholds restricted to each bucket's names. Exploratory decomposition, not a pre-registered hypothesis.

summary: Survivor-only universe, stated as such (audit H1): the OHLCV set holds current listings only, so firms that delisted, merged or were acquired before 2026 are absent
decision: Survivor-only universe, stated as such (audit H1): the OHLCV set holds current listings only, so firms that delisted, merged or were acquired before 2026 are absent. The report, leakage item 14, F04 caption, universe text and the smallest defensible claim say "survivor-only (survivorship-biased)", not "survivorship-aware". S02 writes sp500_coverage.json: the share of fja05680 window members our eligible data covers (ticker-level, approximate).
why: Spec §4 weakness understated by the earlier wording.

summary: Release-EPS parser, third round, from the 2005-2011 real-data run (12 firms, 6 S&P + 6 non-S&P) and a replay over all 3,360 pilot and early-era releases against XBRL: (1) losses: when "loss" (not income / earnings / prof
decision: Release-EPS parser, third round, from the 2005-2011 real-data run (12 firms, 6 S&P + 6 non-S&P) and a replay over all 3,360 pilot and early-era releases against XBRL: (1) losses: when "loss" (not income / earnings / profit) is the nearest results word before the number, the value is negative ("net loss of $25.3 million, or $0.80 per diluted share" was +0.80: 43 of 246 'medium' disagreements were sign errors); (2) sentence starts ignore decimal points (a "$25.3 million" no longer cuts the sentence); (3) plain-text table rows without cell separators ("Diluted $ 0.08 $ (0.05)", common before ~2008) enter the table path with all its filters; (4) EPS stated without "diluted" ("earnings per share were $0.67") forms its own class medium_undiff, ranked after the older patterns so no previously parsed value changes because of it, and admitted to USABLE_CONFIDENCE because its XBRL agreement (80.9%, n=335) exceeds the existing 'medium' class; (5) multi-year summary tables (three or more year headers, no quarter wording) are skipped. Replay result, before the point-in-time full-year check: usable-class agreement with XBRL 78.2% -> 83.9% (pilot, n=2,192), 66.1% -> 83.8% (2005-2011 run); parsed releases +282 (pilot) and +46 (early era). Remaining disagreements include XBRL-side derivation noise (fiscal-year mapping, YTD values), so 100% is not the target.

summary: Point-in-time defect found by the full run's availability assertion (S09): a same-day group of 8-Ks is one event (§5.2) whose features use every filing in it (text, item categories, release EPS / SUE), but its clock star
decision: Point-in-time defect found by the full run's availability assertion (S09): a same-day group of 8-Ks is one event (§5.2) whose features use every filing in it (text, item categories, release EPS / SUE), but its clock started at the group's FIRST acceptance, so a later same-day 8-K's content leaked into a decision time before it was public (5,189 of 141,300 8-K events, 3.7%; the pilot had ~270). The assertion caught it through SUE; the text family's availability was defined at event level, so text could not trip it. Fix (conservative): the group's clock is its LAST acceptance (public, decision, session bucket, T_trade entry, Track A day 0 all follow it); first_acceptance_time is kept for diagnostics; event ids are unchanged. S07 now asserts that no filing in an event was accepted after the event's acceptance time. Unit test with a real 11:00 / 16:50 pair. Pilot results (engineering evidence only) predate this fix.

summary: Hard-rule-7 defect found by the full run's SUE-rule assertion (S09): S06 computes SUE per accession before clusters exist (S07), so when a firm filed its 10-Q minutes after the earnings 8-K on the same day, the 10-Q was
decision: Hard-rule-7 defect found by the full run's SUE-rule assertion (S09): S06 computes SUE per accession before clusters exist (S07), so when a firm filed its 10-Q minutes after the earnings 8-K on the same day, the 10-Q was public within the release's 35-minute decision window and fed the release's SUE history: a same-cluster source. S06 now excludes, for every release, all periodic filings of the firm filed on or after the release within the 120-day cluster window (release_cluster_exclusions, a conservative superset of the D-017 cluster), whatever their acceptance time; the S09 assertion stays as the independent check.

summary: Drift-verdict audit of the full run (hard rule 10: a surprising result opens an audit)
decision: Drift-verdict audit of the full run (hard rule 10: a surprising result opens an audit). SUE-conditioned drift came out at -3.0% (Q5-Q1, CAR4[+2,+60], n=11,885), opposite to classic PEAD. Checks: the SUE sign is right (CAR[-1,+1] rises monotonically from -0.69% in Q1 to +1.14% in Q5) and the reversal holds in every era (2000-08 -1.3%, 2009-16 -3.3%, 2017-26 -3.2%), so it is not a coding error; a survivor-only universe (D-057) biases low-SUE drift upwards and cannot be separated from a genuine large-cap reversal with these data. Two defects found and fixed: (1) (p or 1) < 0.10 treated p = 0.0 as missing, so the one-session-lag check (-3.1%, t=-9.8) and the clean check were scored as failures (robust_same_sign, tested; unknown is None, never 'failed'); (2) overlap flags counted a release's own cluster 10-Q as contamination, leaving 130 of 46,447 releases 'clean'; cluster members are one information event (§5.2) and no longer flag each other (any other same-firm event still does). Never presented as a PEAD replication.

summary: Accounting-feature defect, found by comparing the 150-firm run with the 500-firm run it was derived from (same firms must give identical features; six did not, in 35-52% of rows)
decision: Accounting-feature defect, found by comparing the 150-firm run with the 500-firm run it was derived from (same firms must give identical features; six did not, in 35-52% of rows). A filing reports the current period and the prior-year comparative at the same public time (10,036 of 10,039 Assets filings), and pit_facts ordered facts by public time alone, so the lookup returned the current or the prior-year value depending on sort order (on the old code even a deterministic input gave last year's value: 80 / 70 / 100 instead of 100 / 100 / 120). Not look-ahead (the value is older, never newer) but stale and run-dependent: total assets, leverage, ROA, revenue, latest quarterly EPS, book-to-market and market cap (shares) were wrong in about half of all events in EVERY earlier run (pilot, 500-firm). Fix: within a filing the newest period wins, and a restated older period filed later never displaces a newer one (newest_period_facts); ties in the as-first-reported EPS and SUE-history orderings are now fully ordered. Test: known answers, 25 random shuffles of fact and event order, and the test fails on the old code. Every earlier result that uses accounting features (L3, L6, size controls) is superseded; SUE and release EPS use separate code and were not affected.

summary: Report v2 for the 150-firm study (owner request: a complete end-to-end report with every visual, step and output)
decision: Report v2 for the 150-firm study (owner request: a complete end-to-end report with every visual, step and output). reports/results_summary.md, .html and .pdf now contain, besides the earlier results sections: a reader's guide and glossary; Part A (hypotheses and what was found, 25-stage architecture, data sources and the 150 tickers by industry, NLP pre-processing with measured counts, events/clocks/targets/labels, features and the ablation ladder, models/encoders/training and the search budget, the RAG and extraction system with its real Qwen output and what could not be evaluated, splits and metrics); section 5a (the real chance level, move-vs-direction AUC, paired lifts by period including the locked test, which S19 does not compute); sections 10-11 (answers to the research questions; known issues, reproducibility and next steps); an appendix with the decision log. Figures are placed inline at their sections (markdown image links, embedded in HTML, inline in PDF) and four architecture diagrams (A01-A04) plus six result charts (R01-R06) were added. Corrections made at report level, not in stage outputs: leakage item 4 is relabelled 'built, not scored' because no stress-fold scores exist; the executive summary names the best STRICT model and the frozen model separately; the chance level is the macro-F1 of shuffled own predictions (about 0.33), not the majority-class baseline (0.19). Found while writing it: the L6-vs-L7 freeze compared scores from two different runs (L6 from S11 on the PC, L7 from S15 on Colab); inside S15 the order reverses (L6 0.3909, L7 0.3898), and LightGBM re-scores differ across machines (80% identical classes), so L6 and L7 are tied and the frozen L7 is on the retrospective leaderboard. No stage was re-run and the locked test was not touched.
